title: Retailer-neutral fulfillment adapter interface with universal list export (P1.11, P1.12)
body:
## Role
A backend engineer defining the boundary every retailer integration must respect.

## Goal
Define the retailer-neutral fulfillment adapter interface with declared capabilities (P1.11) and ship its first adapter, a universal text/JSON/CSV export (P1.12).

## Context
ADR 0001 lists the capability vocabulary. #139 may rename or narrow it (for example `shopping_list_link` for Instacart).

## Deliverables
`grocery_butler/fulfillment/base.py` (interface, `Capability`, `HandoffResult`), a registry, shared adapter contract tests, and `ExportAdapter` producing grouped text, JSON and CSV.

## Concrete examples
`ExportAdapter().create_handoff(plan)` returns the grouped checklist; its capabilities are `{EXPORT_LIST}`.

## Constraints
Core modules never import a concrete adapter; each adapter declares authorization method, operations, freshness and whether a human must act.

## Dependencies
#143.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The household can export any plan for any store.
- [ ] Contract tests run against every registered adapter.
- [ ] An import-boundary test guards core modules.

## Testing requirements
Contract tests; golden-file tests for each export format.

## Out of scope
Any retailer-specific adapter.

## Documentation requirements
README Architecture: Fulfillment adapters; ADR 0001 cross-reference.

## Done-Done (repository requirements)
- Invoke tools through `./scripts/*`, never directly; `./scripts/check-all.sh` exits 0.
- Keep the repository's coverage, typing, lint, security and complexity thresholds; don't weaken any gate.
- No `noqa`, `type: ignore`, disabled checks, test skips or retries added to get green. A flaky test is worse than no test.
- Deterministic contract tests and negative-path tests. Tests use a fake transport; a normal test run never calls Instacart.
- Update the docs and API contracts this change touches in the same PR.
- Review the final diff for Safeway or Instacart coupling in core domain modules (`consolidator`, `pantry_manager`, `recipe_store`, `models`, `pending_actions`).
- The PR body references the epic (#142) and closes this issue.
